title: Differential retention profiles with per-field sensitivity scoring and audit packaging
creator: Evelyn Brooks
description:
Problem: Current retention controls operate at a coarse per-route or per-tenant TTL which makes it hard to meet nuanced regulator requests (e.g., keep PII for 30 days but non-identifying telemetry for 2 years). We need a flexible retention model that can assign differential TTLs to subfields of a request/response, score content sensitivity automatically, and generate tamper-evident audit bundles for legal/compliance evidence requests.

Goal: Deliver a retention engine and UI that supports per-field sensitivity scoring, tenant override profiles, and automated evidence packaging (manifest + hash-chain + export bundle) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. This includes a migration path, retention preview tooling, and instrumentation for cost/SLO impact.

Out of scope: Full redact-and-replace workflows for downstream analytics (handled in a follow-up), and policy authoring UX beyond presets and overrides.
acceptance_criteria: API to register per-route retention profile accepting field selectors (JSONPath) and TTLs at 4 granularity levels: immediate, short, medium, long
Automatic sensitivity scanner that assigns 'sensitivity_score' to extracted fields and maps to TTL via configurable policy
Console UI: retention profile gallery + per-tenant override + retention preview (simulate retention outcome for sample requests)
Evidence export endpoint producing ZIP with request/response artifacts, manifest.json, sha256 hashes, and signed export metadata
Retention enforcement runs across storage backends (S3-compatible/objectstore and encrypted DB) and respects Private/VPC customer keying
Integration tests demonstrating retention deletion, evidence export integrity (hash-chain), and an end-to-end customer flow
Performance impact: median request processing additional latency < 3ms for scoring + non-blocking async retention enforcement
Rollout toggle to enable differential retention per-tenant with metrics for bytes retained, deleted, and export frequency
comments: 2025-03-01 - Evelyn Brooks: Kickoff meeting with Legal, Security, and Eng. Legal prefers explicit per-field retention rather than freeform retention notes. Agreed to include a signed manifest for evidence exports.
2025-03-03 - Marco Li (PM): Scoped initial MVP to JSONPath-based selectors and 4 TTL buckets to avoid open-ended TTL values—helps engineering with storage lifecycle implementation.

2025-03-04 - Rahul Desai (Eng): Raised perf concern: running deep PII detectors inline will increase request CPU. Proposal: lightweight regex + ML classifier in async scoring path; store raw until scanner completes, then apply TTL retroactively or flag for manual review.

2025-03-05 - Legal (Anya Petrov): Reviewed evidence packaging requirements; export must include chain of custody fields (exported_by, export_reason, requested_at, legal_hold_id). Added to acceptance criteria.

2025-03-06 - Design (Maya Chen): Shared console mockup link and initial flows — retention gallery + per-route inspector + preview simulator. Need UX for showing what will be deleted and why (field-level justification).

2025-03-07 - Marco Li: Added dependency on ENG-3491 (storage lifecycle hooks) and ENG-3387 (sensitivity scanner service). Marking security review required. Next step: PRD doc link and implementation RFC assigned to Eng infra.
2025-03-07 - Evelyn Brooks: Noted customer asks from enterprise pilots (finance customers) for cryptographic proof of export; include signature with KMS key id and export hash summary.
rollout_plan: Phased rollout: 1) Feature flag behind tenant opt-in + internal pilot with 3 enterprise tenants; 2) Enable on Dedicated with customer opt-in and Private via upgrade bundle; 3) Post-ship: enable default preset for new tenants. Monitor retention-related metrics and export requests for 2 weeks before broader opt-in.
migration_notes: For existing tenants, provide a 'preview and apply' workflow: sample recent requests -> show proposed field-level TTLs -> apply to historic keys using background re-tagging job. Re-tagging job will annotate objects with TTL metadata and schedule deletions; ensure idempotency and retry on transient storage errors.
